text_fidelity_a: Cammenga Official US Military Tritium Lensatic Compass, Accurate Waterproof Hand Held Compasses with Pouch for Hiking Camping Navigation Survival Backpacking Orienteering My husband has been looking at this compass for awhile.  So, I decided to order it for him for Father's Day. On the day I expected to receive it, instead I got a clear bag from (USPS), the post office. Inside was the pristine padded Prime bag that Amazon had sent the compass in. On the outside of the USPS bag was an apology it also stated the content of the Amazon bag was damaged. I looked at the Amazon bag it looked perfect, no gouges, no scrapes or tears on the outside. I thought how did the compass get damaged, if the bag isn't? Then I noticed the Amazon bag had a perfect cut across the top and then I looked inside, there was nothing - empty! Where is the damaged compass?Then I look at the USPS bag again and read the outside a second time. Just an apology no instructions as what to do. Am I just out the money I spent and now I have no gift too? I contacted Amazon customer service and the representative assured me the compass would be replaced at no cost to me. She told me luckily, that I had contacted them early enough to have the replacement compass sent out that very day. She said she would initiate an investigation, as I requested. This was with tax was nearly a hundred dollar item. I am thankful that they are, as when things are apparently stolen,  it hurts all of us on the cost of things. Amazon, like all companies, can't stay in business, if they are giving away items. I received the replacement compass in plenty of time for a gift on Father's Day. He loves it, it works perfectly. He wanted it because of being able to read it in total darkness. He can't  wait until the fall when he can use it when hunting. Thanks Amazon!
text_fidelity_b: Cammenga Official US Military Tritium Lensatic Compass, Accurate Waterproof Hand Held Compasses with Pouch for Hiking Camping Navigation Survival Backpacking Orienteering

I did way too much research and finally settled on this one. Priorities were weight limits, size, durability, and bounce. The trampoline was easy to install, liked that the spring pull tool is included and is needed. 2 Adults about 40 minutes. The Acon name on the mat points up (goofed on this so had to flip)

Cons- The Premium netting takes 2 persons to put up because of the upper ring. Because of the upper netting frame, looks like it will very timely and hard to take down for snowy winters.

text_fidelity_a:
Augason Farms Dehydrated Cross Cut Celery 1 lb 2 oz No. 10 Can Some Augason Farms stuff I buy as emergency food, some I buy for regular use. If I can price out something in this form that is same price or less than other forms, then I go with this as it can be stored away or kept in my working pantry. I use a lot of Augason Farms, and I've been pleased with this.

Dehydrated celery is a great addition to the pantry. Sometimes I dont have fresh, or I have fresh that went bad, or I dont find it in the store, or what is there looks bad, or price is way outside my budget. Having some dried celery tucked away in my pantry really helps stretch the budget and brings value to my time.

I keep the recipe trifecta on hand, "mire poix": celery, carrot, and onion. I keep fresh, frozen, and dried on hand. Usually used in recipes that will help rehydrate these foods no problem. Celery is very easy to rehydrate. I usually just add to the cooking process and its good to go.

Food scarcity is legit, so if you can stock up when items are on sale, then I recommend to do so. Consider it insurance.

FYI: food and such are sold based on weight, not volume. There is 1lb, 2 oz packed in this #10 can (that reads, "number ten" not "ten pound"- it is a size of can). Using a #10 can means that it provides uniformity among storage. Emergency supplies are packed for long term and are packed to stack. They also float. They can be repurposed. Even if one gets a dent, contents are still good (unless and actual hole, which is not likely to happen). The food will not be filled to the brim, and also.. food settles after packing.
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Dehydrated Cross Cut Celery 1 lb 2 oz No. 10 Can

text_fidelity_a: SABRE Stun Gun 3-In-1 Safety Tool, 1.154 Microcoulombs (µC) Charge, 115 dB Personal Alarm, Audible Up To 1,000-Feet (305-Meters), 70 Lumen Flashlight, Includes Wrist Strap While tempted I haven't zapped myself with this and none of my friends are willing to let me test this on them. It does make a reasonably loud zappy sound when you trigger it but I have no idea how effective it is. What I can report having tested are the flashlight and siren. Flashlight at full charge is good enough to help you find a lock in the dark or something you might have dropped but it's not very bright or focused. Just a dim widely spread beam. I don't think the siren would do much to frighten a criminal away, it's barely loud enough to be annoying. A mugger is likely to just hit you and take it away. It might work as a signal device if you fell and needed help. Another problem with this is all three switches; light, siren and stun gun are pink, the marking icon on the buttons are small and hard to distinguish. In an emergency figuring out which button is which could mean a lot. The siren and stun functionality also have an on/off switch on the base that needs to be activated before either feature can be used (the flashlight function is always available). The big problem with the switch is it stands quite proud of the base and can easily be bumped or nudge on, then you have a live stun gun in your pocket and a button that also easily pressed as you fumble this out of your pocket. I can just imagine resting your hand on your leg and shocking yourself completely by accident. If the 'safety' switch were flush or covered in some way to make it hard to accidentally activate I might have rated it higher. As it stands it's just as dangerous to the owner as it is to a would be attacker, maybe more so.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Stun Gun 3-In-1 Safety Tool, 1.154 Microcoulombs (µC) Charge, 115 dB Personal Alarm, Audible Up To 1,000-Feet (305-Meters), 70 Lumen Flashlight, Includes Wrist Strap

Coleman ComfortSmart Suspension Camping Chair After a month-long search for a balcony chair while visiting too many different stores, I finally found this one at BJ's for $39.99. It is a dream to sit in because the material has a lot of give which makes it very comfortable. What I also like is:

- it has a high back and a slight recline to it
- there's a small cup holder (more for a soda can than anything else) that easily folds out from under the right side of the seat
- it appears to be built very sturdy
- it opens with ease
- the arm rests are comfortable and covered in foam
- the chair comes in a nice carrying bag
- the back (which looks white in the picture on Amazon) is actually clear mesh; like a pair of black pantyhose but very strong.

The only negatives are that the chair is heavy, very tall and has a large footprint. The fact that I kept only one of these chairs when I wanted to keep two speaks volumes since I only buy chairs in pairs. However, this is the most comfortable lawn/balcony/beach chair I ever sat in in my life so forget about any potential visitor he or she can stand on the balcony during a visit instead.

By the way, I must have tried over 30 beach and other folding chairs before I found this one. In fact, I purchased a total of 3 different chairs (in sets of 2) in a state of desperation and took all of them back except for this one. The two Lifetime Comfort folding chairs I purchased at BJs for $19.99 were exceptionally sturdy but too clinical looking even though they were relatively comfortable for a straight-backed chair. I almost kept those but when I saw these I bought 2 at BJs for $39.99 each and compared them to the comfort of the Picnic Time chairs. The Coleman won by a long shot. text_fidelity_a:
DeskCycle Under Desk Bike Pedal Exerciser - Mini Exercise Bike Desk Cycle, Leg Exerciser for Physical Therapy & Desk Exercise - Adjustable Leg and Standard Versions I have previously owned and used the original DeskCycle, and I liked it a lot, but ultimately replaced it with a Magnetrainer (taller version, longer cranks, same company, I owned one before and gave it to a friend), a recumbent and a rotating line of cheaper mini and full-sized exercise bikes. I'm back to needing some rehab, so I needed a smaller crank rotation, and this time I got the DeskCycle 2 so I could try the 1" lower pedal adjustment.

I'm a lot fitter than I was 2 years ago, but I can easily get my heart rate up to where I need it to be without raising the resistance much. Would this be an amazing workout for a bike racer or mountain bike rider? Probably not, but honestly it's good for most people to get some real exercise, and if you use it at a slower speed to keep your legs moving, it'll work for you.

It's worth mentioning that my prior experience with the manufacturer's support is that it's very good. Not only are they helpful, they seem to really know the product and seem to care about making customers satisfied. They were helpful this time, answering my questions about the differences between the DeskCycle and the DeskCycle 2.

I'm loving the DeskCycle 2 so far. It's extremely quiet, the action is extremely smooth, and it turns out I really like the lower position as it's more comfortable to use with my knee issues. Read a book on your Kindle, and the time pedaling goes by without noticing. I use my DeskCycle 2 on a hardwood floor, and not only does it not move while pedaling, it's very difficult to move further away when pushing it away with your feet. I imagine at high resistance it may move away, but I can only use it at lower resistances.

I figure my calorie burn by heart rate, age, weight, etc, so I don't mess with the online calorie counter. Basically I don't need the monitor at all - my phone can time my rides, and my heart rate monitor tells me when to speed up or slow down. But I still enjoy checking the numbers, so I'm happy that the monitor comes off and lets me put it where I find it most useful. The online calorie calculator is very low compared to what literally every calculator and heart rate monitor I own reports, but it does show some other interesting data. I will continue to log my calories burned at MFP using other means. Not a problem.

Regarding a few of the negative reviews, I'm puzzled. The people who got a used return from Amazon, why didn't they exchange it? Amazon is great with returns and exchanges, and it makes no sense to give the product a lower review because someone at Amazon messed up. Some of the people who say this is noisy may have put the pedals on wrong, but I keep wondering why they don't just contact customer service to have the issue fixed rather than feeling done to, keeping a bike they're not happy with and writing a negative review. Nothing is perfect, no matter how much you spend - sometimes parts have issues, but this bike has a warranty and good customer service. I've owned 4 mini bikes from 3D Innovations, and every one was very quiet.

If you're like me - rehabbing your knees and ankles, and needing a smaller range of motion - or if you want to use an exercise bike under your desk or while watching TV, in my opinion, the DeskCycle 2 is a great option. If you don't need the pedals to be at their very lowest setting, you can save a few bucks by getting the DeskCycle, but I'm glad I got the version 2. For my needs - and I realize everyone has different needs - the DeskCycle 2 is the best of the many underdesk, folding, recumbent and upright exercise bikes I've owned. It's on the heavy side, but that helps keep it from sliding on the floor. I'm happy I got this, and my knees thank me ;-)

I also purchased a similar ball, [[ASIN:B00374O8JK 9" Body Back Ball & Pump]], so I will be comparing the two balls in this review.

The Overball that I have looks like the blue one pictured above. Although you can't quite see this in the photo, the surface of the ball is covered with slightly raised dots; this improves the ball's gripping surface, making it easy for the Overball to stay in place under your back, behind your knee, etc. The Overball comes with a small, short plastic straw to inflate it and a small plastic pin to use once the ball is inflated. The ball fills up easily enough with the straw; I found that the inflation process took only a minute or so. The problem I had was when I went to insert the pin. The Overball does not retain air very well at all, so every time I tried to insert the pin, the ball deflated almost completely in the brief moments it took me to get the pin in place. I had to repeat the process several times; finally, I inflated the Overball way beyond the point where I wanted it to be, put the pin in as quickly as I could, and was satisfied with the results. I did not have this same problem when inflating my Body Back Ball (which comes with its own nice little hand pump); that ball definitely seemed to hold the air better to allow for pin placement.

In terms of actual performance, I have had no problems with the Overball. It does seem a little squishier than my Body Back Ball, but that might be because of the inflation issues--if you are looking for a firm ball, this is definitely NOT the right choice! But for use with Pilates and other core workouts, where a slightly deflated ball is desirable, the Overball works quite well, and I would recommend it overall.

text_fidelity_a:
Gaiam Sol Sticky-Grip Yoga Mat (5mm) I admit, I have a bit of a "thing" with trying new yoga mats. I have a mat that I love and that I use for most purposes, including practicing both at home and in class, which is my [[ASIN:B00AB3LLVS Manduka eKo Lite Yoga Mat]]. However, I also own other mats I use for other purposes, such as keeping one at work, one for Pilates, etc.

I was interested in this Gaiam mat because it is thicker than my eKo Lite, 5mm as compared to 3mm. Although I like my think Manduka, I thought than the thicker Gaiam mat might be good for occasions when I have to practice on particularly hard flooring. Upon unrolling the mat, I did like that it was thick but FIRM--i.e., it was not squishy. This mat is designed to be two-sided. The first side, which has a texture, is described as the more "traditional" side. At first, I thought that this side would provide more stability, but as soon as I stepped on it, I found that my feet were sliding around.

Given this, I decided to try the mat on the smooth side, which is the design side. This side definitely had more of a "sticky" feel. Upon first use, my feet felt secure upon the mat: the mat did feel like a "sticky mat," and my standing poses felt good. Therefore, I decided to take the mat with me to yoga class the next day, which was a free class held in a room with concrete floors. Just getting the mat there was a bit of a feat, as 1) the mat was a VERY tight fit in my [[ASIN:B000VW4VWA Manduka MatSak Yoga Bag]] (designed for full-size Manduka mats), and 2) the mat is much heavier than my eKo light. But worse, taking the mat to class was a mistake. Initially, standing poses were okay, but my hands continually slid on the mat in down dog. Furthermore, as the mat got a bit sweaty, it just got more slippery and felt quite unsafe.

This is a pretty mat and feels to be very high quality. I may continue to use it at home for Pilates and abs work, but due to stability problems, I cannot recommend it for yoga.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Sol Sticky-Grip Yoga Mat (5mm)

text_fidelity_a:
Empower NiteBright Ultra-Reflective Fittens I purchased a black pair of these gloves at Marshall's for $4.99 ($10 off the current Amazon price) so that I have something reflective on when I walk in the dark of night. Although, I do wear blinking lights on my backpack and one on my cap, I wanted something for the body other than wearing a vest.

On the positive side, these gloves are thin but have a felt interior that keeps my hands warm when walking. They are like texting gloves but without any finger slots. Four fingers slip through the top and the thumb through the side and all fingers remain exposed. What I don't like about them is that both my friend who I walk with and I do not find these particularly illuminating. When a car's headlights hit them, the design on the gloves are supposed to reflect back. However, they are only mildly reflective in my opinion. Had I known this I actually wouldn't have purchased them even at the low price of $4.99.

Kulie AllSport Bicycle Trunk Bag 38L Waterproof Pannier Bag for Front Rear Bike Rack Pannier Bags for Rear Seat Cargo Bag Rear Pack Trunk Pannier Handbag Saddle Bag for Bicycle Front Rack I have mixed feelings about this bag, with some positive and negative features

One issue is its attachment, which is via six velcro straps--two on the bottom and one on each corner/side. On the one hand, that means it's pretty universal, so you don't have to worry if it can go on your rack. On the other hand, it isn't 100% universal, and it's also nowhere near as solidly attached as most high-level bags. On my rack, for instance, the two bottom velcro straps don't work very well--the one toward the seat has little way to attach and due to having a seat bag, it's also tough to get my fingers in there. The four side ones aren't an issue, but with all the straps attach, I can't say I feel wholly confident with just how strongly it is attached to my bike. There's still some movement, and you'll most likely really want to be sure your bag is balanced, which isn't something I worry about with any of the my other biking bags. Honestly, I'd probably bungy the bag to feel wholly confident. Being velcro, I'd also be concerned about how well they'll maintain their attachment abilities over time and weather. In short, it's an inexpensive and more universal way to go, but it offers nowhere near the stability, immovability, or confidence as better attachment modes

The storage is nicely flexible, with a number of pockets and a removable separator in the main compartment, which is nicely padded. The fold-out exandable pockets are a nice touch, and I think will generally be quite convenient for lighter goods. My 16' MacBook isn't going to fit, and even if it did, I'd be worried about its weight over time, and about the lack of padding. I now it says it can handle "laptops", but I'm not super confident about that. But certainly my iPad will go in with room to spare and I wouldn't worry about the weight weakening the pocket. Folder, papers, light clothing, or groceries that aren't too heavy could all go in there. I like the number of compartments, the padding on several, and the ability to expand as needed.

The webbing on top is also nice to either attach things to or to hold a jacket or the like, which is does with a good sense of confidence it won't slip out.

If they could improve the attachment mode, this would be a good or very good bag. As is, I'd call it a value bag that is sufficient for non-expensive items, such as for small grocery runs, a bike to the park where you're carrying a disc and some food and drink, etc.
text_fidelity_b: Kulie AllSport Bicycle Trunk Bag 38L Waterproof Pannier Bag for Front Rear Bike Rack Pannier Bags for Rear Seat Cargo Bag Rear Pack Trunk Pannier Handbag Saddle Bag for Bicycle Front Rack

text_fidelity_a:
EvoShield PX3 NOCSAE Soccer Shin Guard Not sure how these worked so well for everyone, happy for others, but a word of caution. Any other shin guard you can sort of try on in the store or whatever. This one, if they end up not working for you, say goodbye to your $$. You will not know what they are like until you open them, and then you own them.

Test case, U15BP player. We ordered based on sizing on the EvoShield website. Turns out the size chart on the package is different from that on their web site. We ordered too large based on this discrepancy. Sent those back on our dime and ordered a size smaller-- again shipping on our dime, so already out $10-12. My son now on the top end of the size range, meaning the product ought to be approaching too small. Molding went just fine. But final product is simply too big, we knew this the minute they came out of the sleeve but by then we owned them. These shin guards are huge, top to bottom, side to side, and too thick. Watched him trying to play soccer and these shields are damaging his traps and touch, the ball contacts these guards low on his legs and the edges are so thick, there is surface all around his leg that "catches" the ball while maneuvering, resulting in all manner of unfortunate ball contact.

Have calipers here... thickness is 7/16" ! And everyone claiming these are lightweight must not have bought shin guards since 1975. These easily weigh twice our cheap Nike guards. Will they protect you? Must say they will, but then so would a full leg cast and it might have better touch.

Other manufacturers going to ever lower profile guards, these going the other way... now we own a pair of $50 doorstops, maybe we can donate them. No returns on opened product (these are in foiled sealed packages). Is that a worthwhile risk for reinventing something that did not really need reinventing ?

text_fidelity_a:
Huffy Disney Princess Scooter, Pink/Purple, 6-Inch The Huffy Disney Princess Scooter is a steel- framed scooter designed to help youngsters get used to the scooter concept before they move on to the two- wheeled variety. This warm- up scooter features the immensely popular Disney Princess theme, making it an instant hit with young girls everywhere.

The Huffy Disney Princess Scooter is sold disassembled with the pieces in a small box. Putting everything together isn't too difficult, but the process would be much easier if the instructions were clearer. The instructions don't walk you through the assembly process step by step. Instead, they show you a diagram with the different parts pulled apart from the scooter so that consumers can see what goes on first, second, third, etc. This eventually works, but it would have been much better if the instructions were step- by- step and if the images were larger.

As for the product itself, it offers a large footplate with a no- slip design and it has a very cute appearance that young girls will love. I like the skateboard- size footplate and the sturdy, steel frame. The third wheel is nice because it keeps the scooter steady while kids learn how to ride and maneuver. Parents don't need to worry so much that their little one will fall off- the third wheel helps keep the scooter upright while in use.

The Huffy Disney Princess Scooter has adjustable handlebars, but adjusting the height takes a little bit of work and it is possible that some of the other parts will fall off as you make your adjustment. This is another area where the scooter deserves a small amount of criticism. One example is the flimsy plastic piece that acts as a guard and is placed over the handlebar- adjustment bolt. It doesn't lock into place very well and is easily moved around. Then, there is the adjustment bolt itself. It is somewhat annoying to work with because there is almost no clearance space. The nut and washer that go on the end leave almost no space to thread and tighten the bolt.

The Huffy Disney Princess Scooter is a cute, fun scooter that offers safety while preparing youngsters for the day when they decide to graduate to the two- wheeled variety. It isn't perfect, for the reasons stated above, but it does have many good qualities and my little girl loves it. These positive qualities are reason enough to consider making this purchase for your preschool age child.
text_fidelity_b: Huffy Disney Princess Scooter, Pink/Purple, 6-Inch

Large, Black. 010-01847-03 I love the app. It’s super user-friendly, and offers clear menus with your collected info, with options to connect with social media, plot running trails, and find popular places to walk/jog. If I were reviewing this solely on the app, this product would easily earn five stars,

BUT....

The data is 100% off. This is probably the most inaccurate fitness tracker I’ve used so far, both for step counts and sleep tracking. I used it for a little over a week to see if it could “learn”, or if different activities tracked more accurately, and it was pretty inconsistent.

Steps: I set a goal of 7,000 steps, which with my other trackers was a High goal. I could teach/take 3 hours of cardio-heavy dance and have regular activities other than that like cleaning up the house, doing office stuff, checking mail, etc, and I would *sometimes* get to 7,000. That’s Three Hours of cardio. Meanwhile, the last week has been full of house renovating, but that mostly consisted of staying in one place and repairing things, organizing things, and making runs to the hardware store. It did NOT consist of many steps or a bunch of walking. Even so, it said I made it to something around 9,000 steps. There is No Way I took that many steps. If I had to guess, I *maybe* made it to 5k. All week has been the same, with Very exaggerated counts.

Sleep: fail. More than half the nights, it showed no data at all and advised me to wear the band. I have literally not removed this thing even once in over a week, not even for showering. Other nights, it said I slept 8.5 hours, when I know I slept under four. I remembered the time I turned everything off and closed my eyes it was around 4am. I woke up around 8am. The phone said I was asleep by 11:30ish. Another night, it said I slept 10 hours, from 8pm-6-am. I can’t think of a time in the last decade that I’ve gone to bed at 8. I am practically a vampire. And that was on a day I finally got to sleep in, so I woke up at around 11. When I tried editing the data in hopes of teaching it, the system was buggy. I saved and exited the screen, and it went right back to the incorrect stuff. This would happen a few times, and in the end, I was only able to correct one of the nights successfully. I don’t have the energy to keep trying. Maybe it will get better, maybe not, but I’m not doing extra data entry work for this.

So all in all, I can’t recommend this product. The data is consistently wrong, which makes it practically impossible to assess what you’re doing or not doing.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin vívofit 4 activity tracker with 1+ year battery life and color display. Large, Black. 010-01847-03

I filled up the 5 liter one to see what it was like. The plastic is very thin. I was afraid it might burst as I was filling up. It wouldn't hold itself up until it was full. When it's full, water leaks out of the valve from the pressure. Maybe I over filled it, though. I didn't measure the water going in.

After the water level went down, the valve stopped leaking. I put it on the floor and after a few days, I realized that water was slowly spreading across the floor. I put it in a big stew pot (perfect fit) and it continues to slowly leak but not that much. I think the water is actually coming through the plastic but I can't really tell. It will do for an emergency.

If I ever fill up the 15 liter ones, I think I'll have to put them in the bathtub first. I'd be afraid that they might burst and flood my apartment. If you plan to use them for camping and such, I'd pay more for a better quality and thicker plastic.

text_fidelity_a:
BeyondHOME Instant Cabin Tent, 8 Person/10 Person Camping Tent Setup in 60 Seconds with Rainfly, Waterproof & Windproof Tent with Carry Bag for Family Camping & Hiking, Upgraded Ventilation This tent is the perfect size for us as far as we are concerned. My wife and I and two younger sons fit in here with plenty of room to spare. Yes, it's listed as an "8/10 Person Camping Tent", but in reality... those would have to be some very friendly people. That's just the way most all tents are measured. How many people CAN you fit in here. Comfort is not an option at that point. In reality, this would probably sleep 6 people very comfortably, with room for more if needed.

The tent is very easy to set up. Man, have things changed since I was a kid! A tent much smaller than this used to take at least three people, a mule and some very questionable language to put together. Not so with this. Just a few minutes from bag to finished structure, and that's just with one person. With two people (suggested) it's even faster.

There are plenty of windows for looking out, for those who may be mildly claustrophobic, and the open mesh top is perfect for stargazing at night when you don't need the rainfly. The floor is sturdy, but I would always recommend a quality tarp laid down ahead of time just for added protection just in case, no matter what tent you are using. Much easier to replace a tarp than repair the floor of your nice tent.

The removable room divider is great, allowing my wife and I our own "room" while the boys are free to have their own privacy (to a point). It is just a tent after all.

We live in the High Desert of Oregon, so we mostly use it in a dry climate, but this thing does repel water very well and withstands the occasional desert windstorms that come out of nowhere. Out of the box, the waterproofing seems to hold up very well.

You might consider purchasing some more substantial tent pegs, as the included ones are functional but could stand to be better. I'll never judge a tent by its pegs, though. They are what I consider a consumable item while camping. I replace ours when needed, which is fairly often.

Also, if you are going to be in a rainly situation regularly or just want the added security, I always suggest trying to supplement the rainproofing as these things do tend to wear out with time. There are products to seal the seams, floor, tent fabric and let's not forget the rainfly. Do a little searching and decide if it's for you. I'd rather be glad that I did rather than regret not doing it. Waking up in a puddle is never fun, as I can tell you from experience.

Overall, if it's a tent that you are looking for with plenty of room inside, is easy to assemble and take down, and it sufficiently weatherproof, then this tent is probably for you. I know that we have no regrets in our decision to get it. It's a very reliable tool for just "getting away from it all" and enjoying time with family and friends.

Friendly tip: When taking the tent out of the bag for the first time, pay very close atention to how you are unfolding it. Remember this when you are folding it back up to put it away afterwords. This will make it much easier to get it back into the bag. Otherwise, you might have to get that mule again...
text_fidelity_b: BeyondHOME Instant Cabin Tent, 8 Person/10 Person Camping Tent Setup in 60 Seconds with Rainfly, Waterproof & Windproof Tent with Carry Bag for Family Camping & Hiking, Upgraded Ventilation

Back then I had the notion that all camping equipments are pretty much the same that it just all depend son how you use and utilize it. Now for the life of me, I couldn't understand on how I managed to burn frying scrambled eggs which is a No-Brainer for everyone which I cooked on this mess kit.Little did I know that the workmanship of this mess kit is sub par at best: that it's made for beginners and Boys scouts in particular made as their first kit. So I just accepted the fact that I can never fry perfectly good eggs with this until i came to a Army Surplus store  in Berkeley and found my first REAL Military mess kit which is the German Bundeswehr mess kit. It was $9.95 and I said "Why Not!?" I tested that and immediately i found out that having the RIGHT gear really makes all the difference! I fried a couple of scrambled and sunny side up eggs on that mess kit that now I know how to fry it right and it's perfect every time! Right after that, I decide to donate this Coleman mess kit to charity and vowed never again to use inferior-made products. It was worth a little from when I used it but I wasn't satisfied from the results from it. And just like everything else in life...you actually get what you pay for, Using a Military mess kit against this is like night and day difference. My newly acquired German mess kit was clunky, quite heavy but robust, dependable and made just like a Tiger tank! This mess kit was flimsy..just like any other American-made car with a ton issues. This kit is NOT recommended and you would be advise to look for a better mess kit anywhere else.If mess kits is your thing then I would advise to get ANY military made mess kits for they're not only dependable but also "battle-tested" and used in the field. It's nowhere near good enough as-is. Why four stars then? Because for the current listed price of around $25, this is an excellent place to start.

The MOLLE style bag is pretty decent. The kit has lots of items for a variety of purposes. If you start with this kit, you can easily replace items one at a time as needed until you have a perfectly adequate kit. I would start by replacing the flashlight and the knife, as well as the multi-tool. The ones that are included are not going to last very long. But in a pinch, they're much better than nothing.

One thing I like about this kit is that it has a good variety of items in the first aid pouch, instead of just 100 band-aids, it has a smaller but more useful selection of items.

There are certainly much better kits out there, but at this price point this one is better than I expected it to be.

text_fidelity_a:
Square36 Extra Large Exercise Mat 8' x 6' x 7mm Thick. Heavy Duty Gym Mats for Home Workouts Non-Toxic, Non-Slip, For Use With or Without Shoes Exercise Mat - Cardio Workout Mats for Home Gym Flooring. My husband purchased this for me as a Christmas gift to use in my (finished) basement exercise room. We had been wanting to get something to protect our Berber-style carpet and had looked into options such as puzzle mats, but everything seemed to have drawbacks. My sweet husband found this on his own after careful research. He knew that as a yoga teacher, I would want something non-slip for yoga and/or that I could place a yoga mat on top if needed. However, he also knew that I use my exercise room for strength and cardio workouts as well, and so he wanted a mat that would be safe to walk on with workout shoes.

This Square36 Mat fits all of the above criteria! For yoga, it is as non-slip as my best (Manduka) yoga mat. At first, I was still laying down my regular yoga mat over top the Square36 for practicing yoga, but now, I don't usually bother. Because I have the Extra Large size (8 x 6-Feet), I can comfortably practice in any direction I want, which is wonderful! Now that I'm in my late 40s, I love how the mat provides a bit of extra cushion for cardio workouts. (One note: I am a little careful performing pivoting maneuvers on the mat.) As with yoga, I really appreciate that I can perform cardio routines all over the mat, moving in 360-degrees. Finally, the mat is perfect for strength workouts as well. I can place weights--even heavy kettlebells--on the mat without fear of damaging it.

I did not experience any smell with this mat when it was new, and it flattened out easily once I laid it out. On my flat carpet, it does shift a little. There is no actual movement when I am using the mat, but about once a month, I notice that it has moved back maybe 2-3"; it is easy enough to slide it back into its original position. I've now had the mat for six months, and it still looks as good as when I first got it. The only real care I give it is occasional vacuuming (although I might also wipe it down once and awhile with a damp cloth if something seems to have gotten on it). Overall, I think the Square36 is a very good, versatile mat that I would recommend for the exercise enthusiast.
text_fidelity_b: Square36 Extra Large Exercise Mat 8' x 6' x 7mm Thick. Heavy Duty Gym Mats for Home Workouts Non-Toxic, Non-Slip, For Use With or Without Shoes Exercise Mat - Cardio Workout Mats for Home Gym Flooring.

The closed valve again. It easily fit back in travel bag. I mention this as I have had or used different camping air mattresses through the years & sometimes you had to battle a little to get them in their travel bags. It comes with instructions & 3 repair patches. Hoping the patches are not necessary, as it has been my experience that they don’t hold for the long run. Nice air mattress. About 12 inches long & 7 inches wide when folded in bag. Actually was more comfortable than I thought it would be. The one thing that could use a better design is the pump. Directions say open valve & pump with foot. Your foot goes over the hole, so you kind of have to lift your foot a little for it to inflate, if you leave your foot over valve, it doesn’t allow air in to inflate. I think that could of been designed a little better. I also had my son give it a try. He is taller than me & had a few inches to spare, as he may be the one to use it sometimes, nice to know it will still work for him as he grows. Decent air mattress, happy with this order.

text_fidelity_a:
High Sierra Access Laptop Backpack I compared 4 High Sierra backpack models: Access (this model), Neo [[ASIN:B007E7160K High Sierra Neo Backpack]], Mayhem [[ASIN:B007E722MG High Sierra Mayhem Backpack]], and Incline [[ASIN:B007E706K6 High Sierra Incline Backpack]]. I'm a 5'2" woman. For my uses (carryon for travel/day hikes), I selected the Neo model. This pack has alot of extra features, but some are useless. Best added feature of this pack is the raincover. I liked the 2 separate shoulder straps on this model as opposed to the yoke straps on 2 other models. All 4 packs had tags indicating that they could hold a 17" laptop. This model and the Incline could not hold my Dell 17" Inspiron. All 4 packs had pouches in the shoulder straps. The pouch in this one was useless. It was the smallest pouch and did not fit my iphone. Three of the models including this one, had a larger and probably more durable zippers than the Incline model. The padding on the bottom seems the same on all models. The raincover on this Access pack provides some extra padding when the raincover is in the hidden pouch. The padding on the backs of the packs seem to be about the same. I didn't use the packs, so I can't comment on the ventilation/airflow materials at the back of the packs.

Pros:
- Fabric seems durable
- Purple print is great color. Like the black accent.
- Raincover - nice feature. Easy on and off pack. Easy to store in bottom of pack.
- 2 unattached shoulder strips (unlike the yoke straps on other models which I don't like)
- Waist straps can be hidden in area at back of pack when not used.
- Chest straps location can be adjusted up and down about 2 inches
- Back access zipper for getting laptop in/out of pack
- 3 looped Daisy chain for attaching accessories to the front of the pack
- 1 attached Swivel Clip on front for adding gear
- Adjustable side compression straps
- Larger and hopefully more durable zippers on this model (smaller ones on Incline model)
- Comfortable grab handle on top of pack that is not integrated as part of shoulder straps.

Cons:
- Sternum/Chest straps not comfortable location for a 5'2" woman
- Waist straps not comfortable location for a 5'2" woman. Too low.
- Only 1 mesh pocket on outside. Why not add one on other side?
- Mess pocket on holds one 16-20 oz bottles nicely. For 1000 ml nalgene bottle, it stretches too much and doesn't go deep enough to be secure.
- Too Tight of a fit for my 17" Dell Inspiron Computer. (16.5" L x 11.5) Zipper does close at top (barely), but concerned it will cause pack to rip. Fits 15" Dell (15"x10").
- Hard to zip because of the flap over the zippers. If you fold the flap up, then zip the pack, then fold the flap back down, it makes the zipping easier but slower. IMO, this flap is unnecessary since the pack comes with a raincover.
- Detachable pouch for MP3 player or phone (Barely 4"x3"). Concerned it may come off causing whatever is in it to get broken or lost. Pouch is too small for iphone - Velcro closure flap cannot be closed.
- Vapel(tm) mesh Airflow(tm) padded shoulder straps are too stiff and uncomfortably dig into my body
- No zippered side pockets
- Smaller than expected. Fully loaded, not counting the mesh side pocket, it measures 19"x13"x10" = 2470 cu in. Less than the reported 2743.
text_fidelity_b: High Sierra Access Laptop Backpack

Rechargeable Camping Lantern, Collapsible 2200mah Battery Powered LED Lights for Tents, 3 in 1 IP66 Waterproof Emergency Flashlight for Camping, Hiking, Hunting, Outages, Outdoor, Garden I have been trying to get various bug zappers to bring with my family when we go to areas that are not close to a plug. This one is interesting. Let's take a look.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a small box with instructions.

CLOSED
Closed this is used for a light. It has brighter white light, dimmed light and a warning red light.

OPEN
Open this has the ability to zap bugs.

HOW WELL DOES THIS PERFORM?
This performs well as a light, but as a bug zapper, it really is not the season for heavy bugs like we will be having later in the season. I have not been able to catch the few tiny moths in the house, nor the few tiny fruit flies. That is no surprise, however, because this zapper is not very big and these guys have been all over the house.

The light part is nice for using when necessary to see at night. During power outages it also will be handy.

HOW THIS RUNS
This runs not only on USB charging,, but also works with AAA batteries(3) which don't come with it.

CHARGE TIME
This took a couple of hours to charge up fully and it lasts a few hours depending on how it is used. I usually charge after that, so I have not let it run completely down yet.

CAN IT HANG FROM CENTER OF TENT?
This does make a good light for hanging from the center of the tent when you want to see with an overhead light. It also would do well in that position as a bug zapper. It has a handle so you can twist tie it to the loops.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For using at a camp site or on a deck in summer, this is a nice little light to have at the table at night, or use for walking at night around a camp site. As for bug zapper, in the tent, I would have to have some eye masks to sleep with. The light would be too bright for me to sleep with.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. If this turns out to be a bug zapping wonder, I will stop by and update my rating on this zapper/light. As it is now, it works, seems to do what it is supposed to do, but situations are not dire enough to see how good it really is.
text_fidelity_b: Rechargeable Camping Lantern, Collapsible 2200mah Battery Powered LED Lights for Tents, 3 in 1 IP66 Waterproof Emergency Flashlight for Camping, Hiking, Hunting, Outages, Outdoor, Garden

ABUS Mini Ultra 410 Bike U-Lock I really like this lock. I have not had any of the defective shackle problems that some other reviewers are writing about; I hope that they were able to return the product for a replacement or refund. My shackle slides easily onto the U portion. It also slides on in either direction (the keyhole has to face down, but either end of the U slides easily into either hole). These mini-U-locks are great if you always lock your bike to a modern bike rack, which should be designed so the mini-U lock fits easily. The lock fits around the bike rack, my front wheel, and the frame, then you can use a cable or another lock around the rear wheel. The lock is too small to fit around a parking meter, but I never do that now that my city has bike racks all over the place. These mini-U locks are much lighter weight and easier to carry than the full-sized U-locks. This lock only comes with 2 keys so don't lose them (other brands include 3 or 5 keys with their locks). I would prefer a metal bike mount, but this plastic one hasn't failed on me yet. I do like the way the you lock the lock to the mount so it is very secure (no way for it to fall off when you are riding).

This lock has a Sold Secure silver rating, which is done by a well known independent European bike lock testing program. Some locks have a gold rating, but those are all much more expensive and much heavier than this one. A gold-rated lock is appropriate if you lock your bike for long periods of time on the street in a big city with a known bike theft problem (like San Francisco or New York City).

While this lock works great, I'm giving it only 4 stars because there are only 2 keys and also because the comparable OnGuard Bulldog mini-U-lock costs much less on Amazon (and comes with 5 keys).
text_fidelity_b: ABUS Mini Ultra 410 Bike U-Lock

text_fidelity_a:
MSR WhisperLite International Compact Multi-fuel Camping and Backpacking Stove I've had this stove for twenty years. I really like what I've done with the stove, and all the amazing exploits I've had with it might cause me to reminisce fondly of it, but the fact is it leaves a lot to be desired. Yes, it worked to melt snow at extreme altitudes. Yes it worked as nearly my entire kitchen on multi-week treks in the backcountry. Yes, it survived 20 years and still works dependably, sort of.

I can only remember being well and truly frustrated with it one time, on backcountry ski trip. It was storming outside the tent, and I was at high altitude. I only filled the bottle with about an inch and a half of fuel because it was only an overnighter. The bloody thing would not stay lit. After that, I bought a smaller bottle to avoid problems with a low fuel level. I also bought a larger bottle for multi-week trips.

This is a stove that rarely works at its best. Most of the time it manages to work acceptably. Some of the time it works poorly. It was rare that it worked truly bad.

I always used white gas in it. It's fairly efficient so I never had an experience where I ran out of fuel, or if I did, it was inconsequential because it was on the last day or something. I'd be more concerned with running out of isobutane with one of those systems.

This stove system is both finnicky and fragile. It really works well if the stove is in just the right condition, with the bottle filled just the right amount, the stove level, the bottle at the proper angle for the pick-up tube, and at the right pressure.

Despite the stove itself being very tough, the plastic bottle valve doesn't stand up. The replacements are expensive, and the reviews for that replacement show a consensus that these things have problems. I would say the reviews for those replacement pumps are probably more accurate and unbiased than the ones for the stove.

I have a MSR Reactor for a couple years now. It simply blows the Whisperlite away in terms of melting snow or boiling water. It's far simpler, almost stupid-proof, way faster, and practically just as light and compact when you factor the fuel bottle and pot.

More recently, I acquired a Trangia alcohol stove. As a minimalist with a preference for ultralight style, it was appealing. I don't have extensive experience with it yet. I bought it to simmer and cook, which the Whisperlite and Reactor don't do well at all. While the Trangia would be slower to melt snow or boil water (the forte of the Reactor, and Whisperlite), I believe it would still do the job under practically all the conditions I'll encounter. Alcohol is a far more appealing fuel to carry than white gas or isobutane.

At this point, I have a broken bottle valve. It works, but the plastic clips to retain the pump plunger are broken. For less than the price of a replacement part, I acquired the Trangia stove that I will likely use for the next 20 years. It's lighter, cleaner, easier to use, simmers nicely, and takes less space in the pack.
text_fidelity_b: MSR WhisperLite International Compact Multi-fuel Camping and Backpacking Stove

Pelican Self Inflating Sleeping Pad w/Pillow & Arm Rest, Camping Gear - Waterproof Foldable Lightweight Air Mattress - Memory Foam Sleeping Mat for Hiking, Backpacking - Travel Accessories - Black I use Pelican cases for work all the time, so I was intrigued at how they would handle camping gear like this. At first I was a little bit disappointed in the "self inflation" part. But once I understood what it means, I really do appreciate it now.
The only truly inflatable part are the side bars (which prevent you from rolling off the mat) and the pillow part. The middle is just memory foam with a familiar looking Pelican style valve on the bottom. If you've ever bought a memory foam mattress online, you know how this works- it comes in a vacuum sealed bag devoid of air, but once you cut it the air whooshes in and the mattress inflates to normal size. That's sort of what this "self inflation" is. You open the valve, the memory foam inside puffs itself up and becomes a more comfortable mat that is noticeably thicker than it was a moment ago. Seal the valve back up, and you can lie down on it and it honestly feels better than it looks!
Once you are done using it, allow the air to leave the side pockets and pillow, release the valve at the bottom, and roll it up. While rolling it, the air will leave the valve at the bottom, and when you've reached the end, just close the valve again to seal it from trying to open and inflate again. It's actually a pretty smart design once you understand it, I just didn't know what to expect before it arrived. I hope this review helps explain it to future buyers who might be expecting a larger self inflating mattress.
text_fidelity_b: Pelican Self Inflating Sleeping Pad w/Pillow & Arm Rest, Camping Gear - Waterproof Foldable Lightweight Air Mattress - Memory Foam Sleeping Mat for Hiking, Backpacking - Travel Accessories - Black

My normal forms of exercise were also making it worse and so I wanted to see how rebounding would help.
Let me tell you that with just a couple minutes here and a couple minutes there of doing the 'health bounce' alone has made remarkable differences in my hip/knee pain (almost gone); noticeable improvements in the 'elimination' area; and giving me deeper, restful sleep and less irritability. AND, I've even noticed a slimmer tummy!
Now, how can this be??!!! I'm only doing a COUPLE minutes here and there!
Yet, the book and the DVD will explain how this form of body movement affects your body at the deepest level - the CELLULAR level!
With that information - with those results - how is it that people aren't STAMPEDING and buying these things faster than Amazon can sell their KINDLES!!??

I realized I had been in the 'dark' too long to not have known the incredible benefits that rebounding/bouncing does for your health, but not any more!

I can't help but wish that I were able to COMPARE my rebounders bounce/feel with other rebounders of EQUAL or GREATER value in order to see if another would've been more comfortable for me, but I'll not ever have that opportunity to do so; and this was my price range and I am content with it and would recommend it.

text_fidelity_a:
Calming Cozy by Sharper Image Personal Sherpa Wrap with Electric Heating Massaging Vibrating Foot Bed, 3 Heat & 3 Massage Settings for 9 Relaxing Combinations A few important details about the Calming Cozy by Sharper Image:

✔️ Only the foot portion is heated.
✔️ Even on the highest setting, the heat isn’t very hot.
✔️ The massager is a vibrating massager, very basic.

I expected the whole wrap to be heated, but as I noted, only the foot portion is heated. The blanket part is a normal sherpa blanket. The sherpa is warm and cozy, but I feel like calling it a “heating wrap” is a bit misleading when only the foot area heats up.

The first question in the FAQ is actually “Why doesn’t my Calming Cozy feel hot enough?” So that tells me right there that Sharper Image knows this doesn’t get too warm. The answer in the FAQ is to give the Calming Cozy to heat up -- put it on high and wait 10 minutes. I waited 15 minutes, on high temperature, and still didn’t find it too warm. I tested this out on a 70℉ day and I wasn’t too hot.

I did notice the foot portion holds the heat for a while even after it’s turned off.

The foot massager is vibration only. The light setting is so light as to be ticklish. For the medium and high speeds, my mom heard the vibrations and asked what I was doing. So if you wanted to use this in an office, the massager is not super quiet.

The Calming Cozy has a few nice quality-of-life features. There are two velcro cable ties at the top, to hold the remote so you can easily access it. There is a built-in elastic strap to hold the blanket rolled up when you aren’t using it, for easier, compact storage. There is a zipper on the side, to make it easier to get into and out of the wrap.

The heating element can be removed, so that you can wash the sherpa blanket.

I can see myself using the Calming Cozy at my desk in the winter -- but as a foot and leg blanket only. The heat and vibration just aren’t worth it.
text_fidelity_b: Calming Cozy by Sharper Image Personal Sherpa Wrap with Electric Heating Massaging Vibrating Foot Bed, 3 Heat & 3 Massage Settings for 9 Relaxing Combinations

text_fidelity_a:
Retrospec Solstice Trekking & Ski Poles for Men & Women - Aluminum w/Cork or Foam Grip - Adjustable & Collapsible Lightweight Hiking, Walking & Skiing Sticks Good light, sturdy poles. They aren't cheap feeling. I am really quite impressed with the design, how they feel, and the overall options included. They come clipped together (keep the clips, or discard) tucked away in a nylon drawstring storage bag. The kit contains wide and narrow snow baskets and rubber boots/tip. Just screw on. Can choose to use none of those and just use the carbide tip. Can elongate both portions via a clip to your height needs. I am 5'10" and these are plenty long for me. They shorten down to manageable height for easy storage and carry. The carry bag has a shoulder strap.

I have used these for snow shoeing, XC/alpine skiing (not nordic/down hill- these are not meant for that), walking through snow in regular boots, walking in mixed dirt/snow/ice. They are really quite sturdy. They are way better than a pair of basic walking pole/sticks I had that broke on a trail within a couple of uses. I find the ones that are capable for snow use to be better. These are better priced than many too. I would/will recommend these!

My primary use though: I happen to have a long semi steep hill directly outside my back door. We have dogs, so we are always going down that hill to get to more leveled out ground. The soil is sandy and doesn't hold grass well. So we are missing a lot of grass and even where there is grass, it tends to get kicked up easily. So even on dry days it can be a slipping hazard. Now add in rain, mud, ice, snow.. and well you can understand what I am about to say next: trekking poles (and good boots) help. Use of poles add a little additional stability. I like to use mine with the large cups, for this purpose. Our winter thus far in NY has been pretty much spring like. Not enough snow to keep mud/ice at bay, not enough cold to keep things firmed up out there. I want my freezing days, and we have barely had any. No Almost no reprieve from mud and slop. So much potential slippage. So much dirty paw action! Ah well.

Bright spot is getting out to play with my dogs and using these to walk around the yard. I just use them for the hill, but once down to the level area, I mind as well keep on using them.. so in this sense I am getting an additional work out of the sort because I am using my arms to move these. I will continue to use these come spring/summer on my walks for that very reason (which is why I had walking sticks before.. for additional burn)

The product description did a great job describing these and the included pictures are spot on. I included a pics of my dogs on the hill. We aren't even to the bottom yet. You can see a little bit of the back of the house at top of hill. You see that the hill starts immediately. Many people have asked if we go sledding on this hill. At bottom of hill the land levels out for maybe 20 feet and butts up to a creek. The back yard is an adventurous place!-- and these multi use trekking poles are helping me navigate it in a more safe and steady manner. Yay!
text_fidelity_b: Retrospec Solstice Trekking & Ski Poles for Men & Women - Aluminum w/Cork or Foam Grip - Adjustable & Collapsible Lightweight Hiking, Walking & Skiing Sticks

Nautilus R616 Recumbent Bike (Discontinued) This is a very sturdy, easy-to-assemble recumbent bike that is likely to turn out to a solid long-term value at this pricepoint. The only negatives of this bike is the fairly flimsy looking plastic covers for the wheel and a rather too bright LCD panel.

All parts required for assembling are clearly labeled and the instructions (predominantly pictures) are good enough for anyone with some minor experience to put it together in about an hour. The length of the power cord is an important consideration to keep in mind where you plan to keep the bike (would have preferred a longer wire). Packaging is good (tons of packaging material that cannot be recycled though) and the unassembled box will need 2 persons to carry.

Setting up the bike is fairly trivial (though it is difficult or even impossible to reset the time/dates - so, pay attention when you initially set the time/date functions).

Bluetooth works as advertised, no issues in pairing with my devices; speakers are OK (you are not likely to give up your headsets), and the fan may provide more white noise than breeze at lower settings. USB connections seem to charge a bit slow. So, the technology features are not something sensational but represents an excellent value at this price point. The Heart rate display is an excellent feature - (need to test the calibration to confirm accuracy, but I've not done that yet). Based on your heart rate, it displays whether you are in the aerobic or anaerobic zone - giving a good sense of calorie burn rate.

With the relative easy of assembly, excellent options for personalizing your workout and archiving, heart rate monitor with a very useful and intuitive display, ability to connect to your audio devices, a holder for tablet & USB port, this bike represents a compelling value for this price. One wishes the plastic covers were stronger and some of the finishes for the plastic bottle holder and other covers more elegant. 4.5*
text_fidelity_b: Nautilus R616 Recumbent Bike (Discontinued)

Augason Farms Freeze Dried Whole Blueberries 12 oz No. 10 Can Get what you can, while you can. Spend now, or spend even more later (and that is if food is available). Doesn't need to be emergency packed food. Buy extra of what you like to eat every single time you are at the store, shop sales, go frequently (don't wipe out shelves). If you are at a spot where you want to add greater variety to put into long term storage, then Augason tends to have quality products and better prices than other emergency brands. Look for their sales, shop often, build up your supplies.

I like adding blueberries into the mix as it reconstitutes well, has good flavor and texture, and is still loaded with nutrients. Easy enough to stock up on rice and beans, harder to stock up on fruits and vegetables. Grow what you can, freeze or can what you can.. and buy what you can. Freeze dried is a very nice way to get good food that is still nutritious.

Most #10 (that reads, "number ten" not ten pound) cans will maintain freshness and quality for 10-25 years after production date. If opened, it will be shorter; depends on what you get. Blueberries in my experience are perfectly fine for a long time. Environmental factors will impact this. The cans are pest proof, can take a beating (even if dented should be fine as foods are freeze dried and have no moisture to sustain bacterial growth), can float if not opened, and are a standard size for stacking and uniformity (hence why weights will vary, and some stuff only fills a little of can).
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Freeze Dried Whole Blueberries 12 oz No. 10 Can

SurfShelf Treadmill Desk: Laptop and iPad Holder I am using this product with a ProForm Performance 400 Treadmill. I am a walker, not a runner.

Out of the box, it was obvious that this was going to be an easy installation. I slid the end of the straps out of the clasp, threaded them through the back piece, and wrapped them around the console. After closing the clasps, I adjusted the strap lengths to position the back piece on the top of the console.

There was a bit of a hurdle to properly secure the shelf. There is no hinge in the shelf. Instead, you adjust the point where the shelf rests on the back piece's support. It can be a little tricky, but I did not have much trouble getting the shelf to be horizontal. Total time including removing the shelf, reading the instructions a second time to clarify some points and installing it properly was 15 seconds.

The support seems good. I placed a Dell XPS laptop on the shelf. I was able to secure it with the strap, and the shelf felt stable. I was playing movies most of the time, but I also did some typing and scrolling with the touch pad. I was also easily able to partially close the laptop to see the top of the console.

PROS:
Easy installation
Works as advertised
No need to make your own shelf that may or may not work
Good size to provide solid support to even large laptops
Easily adaptable to many exercise machines

CONS:
A bit pricy for what you get, but then you save time and money making a shelf
Obscures the console, but I can still reach under the shelf to get to the controls okay
I do not see it working well with a tablet
The strap that holds the laptop covers some of the controls and keyboard (YMMV on this one)

OVERALL:
This was a good buy. This should be something that I use daily for years.
text_fidelity_b: SurfShelf Treadmill Desk: Laptop and iPad Holder

text_fidelity_a:
SOG Specialty Knives SAT002-BX Flashback Tini Knife, Black SOG has been in the industry a long time. They offer an affordable value in the knife world. They constantly try to innovate and carry Lifetime Warranties on their products. Some of their designs are fantastic. Some are duds. The Flashback is an awesome every day carry folder that is nearly perfect but just misses shy. I still managed to pick up this straight clip model as well as a tanto version.

Packaging: This is the black box version. Not the retail box version. It doesn't matter, you get the same knife in both boxes but one doesn't have a clear window to view the blade and the other is just a black manufacturer's box that says SOG. It's not about the box, it's about what's inside.

First glance: This thing screams cool. I just love the color scheme, look of the blade, the total design reminds me of a slick silver on black race car set up. The clip is reversible, but already comes in my preferred carry designation. It rides deep in the pocket and retains firmly to the pocket. I haven't had one instance of it coming loose or getting hung up on seatbelts or the like in my daily use.

Picking it up: I believe SOG advertises these Flashback knives around 3.8 oz. It feels heavier, but I don't have a scale to confirm. Either way, it's fairly light. Disable the safety, and then never use it again. I'm actually of the mindset SOG should just delete their safeties on most of their assisted folders, but your mileage may vary. If it gives you a warm fuzzy to use it, then do so. I think it just takes away from the attractiveness of the design and is unnecessary. First use flicking it open and you realize SOG really meant this thing was fast. It opens authoritatively, too, so hold on to it. Snaps into a firm lock position and is ready to use. The blade is AUS-8 steel and comes hair shaving sharp out of the box. AUS-8 is OK, but I wish SOG would use some better steels in their builds. It'll be fine for the use of everyday carry, however. I'm not a huge Tanto fan, but I had to have that model in addition to this straight clip Flashback I picked up due to how much I liked the straight clip after carrying a few days. The Tanto was supposed to be a gift, but I think I'm keeping it, too. As for the grip, you can get a firm purchase on the blade as a result of the aggressive gimping. I think SOG nailed this one unlike some of their other designs. It fits my hand so well and provides a level of confidence in use as result.

Build Quality: Now here's where things get tricky. SOG is a mass market knife maker. Meaning they pump them out, check on the quality so often, and use cheap labor to build it. One example can be outstanding in build and the next will be ok for the value. The tanto I received has perfect blade centering. The straight clip model is off to one side. Both are well built, but inherent in a lot of SOG designs there is some side-to-side play in each once the blade is in the locked position. It has something to do with their locking design as it was also inherent in the Aegis I've previously owned. This is where I knock these knives down a star as others in the same price category like Cold Steel and Spyderco don't have these issues.

Overall: I love carrying this knife. I do prefer the straight clip blade design and would recommend that to purchasers as the blade shape is more useful, at least to me. I still had to have this tanto version in addition. There are some caveats that come in the mass-produced build quality, but if you want a well-built everyday folder that has a solid value than you shouldn't be disappointed in the Flashbacks from SOG. I would suggest shopping around a bit and making sure you do get the best price, however, as these can fluctuate. With a few shortcomings, this still comes as a recommended buy.
text_fidelity_b: SOG Specialty Knives SAT002-BX Flashback Tini Knife, Black
